Neue Grafik journal

The trilingual Zürich journal that stated the style’s principles and printed them as a four-column grid on every cover.

Made
1958–1965
Style

Moods

Rights

Context

Neue Grafik was a quarterly founded in Zürich on 15 February 1958 by Josef Müller-Brockmann, Hans Neuburg, Richard Paul Lohse, and Carlo Vivarelli. Eighteen issues appeared from 1958 to 1965. Wikipedia: Neue Grafik.

Issue 1, September 1958: letterpress, 28 × 24.8 cm, 75 pages, published and printed by Verlag Otto Walter AG, Olten; cover design Carlo Vivarelli. eMuseum object 23096, cover, object 44032.

The eMuseum description of issue 1 notes Akzidenz Grotesk for the headings and Monotype 215 for the texts, and a cover of four columns in which only the issue number changes. eMuseum object 44032.

Wikipedia notes the journal’s advocacy of photography as a central element of graphic design, and criticism in Zürich that the style was rigid and cold. Wikipedia.

Observed

  • Issue 16 cover: the three-language title stacks in three lines of large black grotesque at top left, tightly spaced.
  • Below the title, the page divides into four columns: contributors’ names in the first, then German, English, and French contents in parallel.
  • The issue number “16” is the only other large element, set in the first column at the same size as the title.
  • Everything is black on white and flush left; there are no rules, images, or color.
  • Large empty bands separate the title, the subtitle row, and the contents.

Why it belongs

The cover is a table of contents made into a composition. It demonstrates the style’s claim that correct organization of information is itself the design.

The fixed template, with only the number changing, treats the journal as a system rather than a series of individual covers.

Borrow

Use parallel columns for parallel languages or versions, aligned line for line.

Design a fixed cover or page template where a single variable, such as a number or date, carries the change.

Let the table of contents be the hero of an index page.

Published by the editors of Der Film and set in Akzidenz-Grotesk.
